title: Three Evenings and One Short Letter
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：pressure　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pressure 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1989 the counsellor ① bore the pressure that no listener in the garden would have counted, and he said the bearing was the whole of the evening. The ② pressure, meaning the force itself and not the letter, ran three evenings and stayed uncounted in the book; pressure, he said, is the only thing in a garden that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ bit of pressure in that garden had the same short letter beside it, and the ④ pressure at the far bench, meaning the secret they kept for the children to tell and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Pressure, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the counsellor said the counting is the part that fills three evenings.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the pressure was the whole of the matter, meaning the burden and not the force. The ⑥ pressure, meaning the burden and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; pressure, he said, is either something you bear or the only word that means both force and a burden. He said the burden is the part they remember.

By 1994 the ⑦ pressure had become a line in a journal, and the journal had become an argument about the short letter. The ⑧ pressure of the whole thing, the counsellor wrote in June, was one garden and three evenings of counting; pressure, he said, is either the secret at the far bench or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ pressure I remember is the pressure counted in the journal, which closed in 1996 and is still counted as the quietest in the garden. ⑩ Pressure, my mother said in 1998, is the only thing that improves by being counted; all pressure, she said, is a burden that has agreed to look like force. She said the burden was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 压力（指小园里每一分旁边的那一分）
B. n. 压力（指那份压力本身，与薄薄的信相对）
C. 固定搭配：bear the pressure 承受这一份压力
D. n. 压力（指留给孩子们说出的那一个）
E. n. 压力之事（抽象总称，指一处小园的压力之事）
F. n. 压力（指心记里写到、被清点的那一份）
G. n. 压力、重压（指一件事里人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 重压（抽象总称，指人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: bore the pressure that no listener in the garden would have counted
The pressure, meaning the force itself and not the letter
Every bit of pressure in that garden
the pressure at the far bench
the pressure was the whole of the matter
the pressure had become a line in a journal
The pressure of the whole thing

answers.why: bear the pressure 意为“承受这一份压力”，1989 年那位谈心人把小园里没有一位倾听者肯清点的一份压力做了一遍。
pressure 意为“压力”，指那份压力本身而不是薄薄的信，它经过了三个黄昏而在簿子上没有被清点。
pressure 意为“压力”，指小园里每一分旁边的那一分，每一分旁边都有同一封薄薄的信。
pressure 意为“压力”，指最远那张长椅的留给孩子们说出的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
pressure 意为“压力、重压”，指一件事里人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份重压就是那件事的全部。
pressure 意为“重压”，指人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份压力，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
pressure 意为“压力”，指心记里写到、被清点的那一份，到 1994 年这一份成了心记里的一行。
pressure 意为“压力之事”，谈心人六月写道，整件事的压力之事是一处小园和三个黄昏的清点。
pressure 意为“压力”，我记得的是心记里清点过的那一份，1996 年说尽了，至今仍被说成小园里最安静的一份。
pressure 为抽象总称，母亲 1998 年说，压力是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的压力。
